evals.prompt: Rewrite the hero copy for Ledgerline, a B2B analytics tool for product managers at subscription companies. Our difference: it shows which step of the signup funnel loses the most users, refreshed every hour, with no engineering setup. Current hero: headline "Ledgerline: Powerful analytics for modern teams", subhead "Everything you need to make data-driven decisions, seamlessly", buttons "Get started" and "Learn more". There is no voice guide yet.
evals.expected_output: An assumed voice brief at the top, then a string table with a headline that passes the specificity test with the brand name removed (names the funnel-step finding, product managers or subscription companies, and the hourly or no-setup difference), a subhead with one promise, and two buttons that are each a verb plus an object. The old strings appear as before values with the rule each one broke.
expectations: Puts a four-line voice brief (audience, register, three never-words, one sentence the brand would say) at the top and marks it assumed

The new headline, with "Ledgerline" removed, names what (which signup step loses users), for whom (product managers or subscription companies) and the difference (hourly refresh or no engineering setup), and does not use powerful, modern, seamless or data-driven

Both buttons are a verb plus an object (for example "See your funnel" rather than "Get started", and "Read the setup steps" rather than "Learn more"), and the primary button's object matches what the user gets next
The subhead makes one promise; the other claims become section headings or are cut
Uses no number, customer or guarantee that the prompt does not supply, and writes [needs a fact: ...] where a rule asks for one
Delivers a string table with location, before, after and the rule applied, and reports a detector count before and after

evals.prompt: Write the state microcopy for the order basket in a mobile ordering app for Marlowe's, a single independent cafe. Regulars order on their phone so the drink is on the counter when they arrive; the cafe says drinks take about 6 minutes. The basket loads from the server, can be empty, can fail when the card is declined or the phone goes offline, confirms the order, and lets the user cancel an order the counter has already started. The cafe never uses the words "seamless", "journey" or "experience".
evals.expected_output: A loading, an empty, two error, a success and a confirmation string for the basket, each under 12 words, each with the required parts for its state, in a plain counter-side register, with the 6-minute figure used in the success state and the confirmation button repeating the verb and object.
expectations: The loading string names what is loading (the basket or the order), not "Loading..." or "Please wait"
The empty string says why it is empty and gives a next step that names a thing (add a drink, see the menu), not "No items"
The card-declined error says what happened and gives at least one way out (another card, pay at the counter), without "Something went wrong", "Oops" or blame
The offline error says the order was not sent, what is kept, and when or how to retry, not "Try again" alone

The success string says the order was sent and uses the 6-minute figure from the prompt rather than an invented time, and the confirmation names the consequence (the counter has started it) with a button that repeats the verb and object, never "Yes" or "OK"
Every string is under 12 words, and none contains seamless, journey or experience

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.

Learn more

Features

Fast

Your text here

Simple

Powerful tools for modern teams.

evals.expected_output: A sweep table with one row per hit (location, string, tell, fix or [needs a fact]), a count of tells against a count of strings, and no rewritten page, because the prompt asked for the sweep only.
expectations: Flags the lorem ipsum paragraph, "Your text here", alt="image", "Learn more", the example.com address and the 555 number as placeholder tells
Flags the <title> "Home" as a document default and the h2 "Features" as equal to its nav label
Flags "Fast", "Simple", "Secure" as a three-item list of vague parallel words, and the repeated adjectives powerful and simple across the cards

Does not rewrite the page or invent facts for the fixes; fixes without a source read [needs a fact: ...]

evals.prompt: Our founder wrote this headline and it is final: "Bloom: The smarter way to manage your garden". Write the rest of the hero for Bloom, a reminder app that tells home gardeners in Ireland what to sow, feed and prune each week, based on their postcode's frost dates. We need a subhead and one primary button. Keep the founder's headline.
evals.expected_output: The founder's headline delivered word for word in the string table, a subhead and a button that pass the rules, and a separate Proposed changes block that shows the headline fails the specificity test (with the brand name removed it fits any garden app, and "smarter" does the work), proposes an alternative, and leaves the decision to the owner.
expectations: The delivered headline is exactly "Bloom: The smarter way to manage your garden", unchanged
A separate Proposed changes block gives the original, a proposal, the rule it failed (specificity test or the adjective "smarter") and one line of reason, and says the owner decides
The proposal is not mixed into the delivered strings and is not presented as applied
The subhead names what (weekly sow, feed and prune reminders), for whom (home gardeners in Ireland) or the difference (postcode frost dates), and makes one promise
The primary button is a verb plus an object that matches what happens next (for example entering a postcode or seeing this week's jobs), not "Get started"
No invented facts: no plant count, user count or price appears unless the prompt gave one
